# gpcn_vpc_nsg (Resource)

Manages a network security group inside a GPCN VPC, with its rules inline. GPCN replaces the whole rule set on every change and identifies a rule by its content, so the rules belong to this resource rather than to one of their own. The API key needs vpc:read to read a group, and vpc-nsg:create, vpc-nsg:update and vpc-nsg:delete to manage one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: A network security group for a GPCN VPC
#
# The rules live inline. GPCN replaces the whole rule set on every change.
# GPCN identifies a rule by its direction, protocol, port range and remote
# CIDR. A rule therefore has no identity of its own to manage separately.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    gpcn = {
      source  = "Global-Private-Cloud-Network/gpcn"
      version = "~>1.4.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "gpcn" {
  host = "https://api.gpcn.com"
}

# Lookup datacenter in Central US region
data "gpcn_datacenters" "central_us" {
  country_name = "United States"
  region_name  = "Central"
  name         = "Chicago"
}

resource "gpcn_vpc" "example" {
  name          = "terraform-demo-vpc"
  datacenter_id = data.gpcn_datacenters.central_us.datacenters[0].id
  cidr          = "10.60.0.0/16"
}

resource "gpcn_vpc_nsg" "example" {
  vpc_id      = gpcn_vpc.example.id
  name        = "terraform-demo-web"
  description = "Web tier posture"

  rule {
    direction      = "ingress"
    protocol       = "tcp"
    port_range_min = 443
    port_range_max = 443
    remote_cidr    = "0.0.0.0/0"
    description    = "HTTPS from anywhere"
  }

  # Ports apply to tcp and udp only. Omit them for icmp and all.
  rule {
    direction   = "ingress"
    protocol    = "icmp"
    remote_cidr = "10.60.0.0/16"
    description = "Ping from inside the VPC"
  }

  rule {
    direction   = "egress"
    protocol    = "all"
    remote_cidr = "0.0.0.0/0"
    description = "All outbound traffic"
  }
}

# Bind a subnet to the group
resource "gpcn_vpc_subnet" "example" {
  vpc_id = gpcn_vpc.example.id
  name   = "terraform-demo-web"
  cidr   = "10.60.1.0/24"
  nsg_id = gpcn_vpc_nsg.example.id
}

output "gpcn_vpc_nsg_example" {
  value = gpcn_vpc_nsg.example
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable name for the security group. It must be unique within the VPC
- `vpc_id` (String) Unique identifier of the VPC the security group belongs to. Changing this value requires replacing the security group

### Optional

- `description` (String) Additional information about the security group to provide context for its purpose
- `rule` (Block Set) One traffic rule of the security group. GPCN identifies a rule by its direction, protocol, port range and remote CIDR, so two rules that agree on all four are the same rule (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) Timestamp when the security group was created
- `failure_reason` (String) Why the last operation on the security group failed, or null when none has
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the security group in UUID format
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the VPC's own default security group. GPCN creates that group with the VPC and refuses to delete it
- `last_updated` (String) Timestamp when the security group was last updated
- `rule_count` (Number) The number of rules the security group holds
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state of the security group: one of 'creating', 'ready', 'failed' or 'removing'
- `subnet_count` (Number) The number of subnets bound to this security group. GPCN refuses to delete a group while this count is above zero

<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `direction` (String) Direction the rule applies to: either 'ingress' or 'egress'
- `protocol` (String) Protocol the rule applies to: one of 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp' or 'all'
- `remote_cidr` (String) Remote address range the rule applies to, given as an IPv4 CIDR at its network address (e.g., 0.0.0.0/0 or 203.0.113.0/24)

Optional:

- `description` (String) Additional information about the rule. GPCN edits it in place, because it is not part of the rule's identity
- `port_range_max` (Number) Highest port the rule applies to. Ports apply to the tcp and udp protocols only, and must be given together with port_range_min
- `port_range_min` (Number) Lowest port the rule applies to. Ports apply to the tcp and udp protocols only, and must be given together with port_range_max

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A security group is read through its VPC, so the import ID names both:
# "<vpc_id>/<nsg_id>".
terraform import gpcn_vpc_nsg.example "c13808d9-3b7d-42c5-a21d-f0961308a38a/4a6c1f38-92b1-4e77-8d50-6f3c2a1b7e94"
```
